SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r5.claim: Benefit is restricted because people seek it for themselves; harm is unrestricted because one may wish it for an enemy or fear it for oneself.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p718/r5.anchor: النفع يريده الإنسان لنفسه أما الضرّ فلا يريده الإنسان لنفسه إنما يُريده لعدوّه

DAMGHANI:v1p289/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r6.claim: Ḍarr can mean harm in the ordinary sense.
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r6.anchor: الضر بعينه اي الأذى قوله تعالى في سورة الشعراء

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.claim: Abraham’s questions expose the idols’ baselessness; the people have no answer and persist only because they follow their forefathers, a tradition they will not abandon.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r4.anchor: because they are only following the ways of their forefathers, which they will not give up at any cost

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.claim: The reported events occur after Abraham had conclusively conveyed the truth through both scriptural and intellectual arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p420/r5.anchor: when he had conclusively communicated the truth to his people through both scriptural and intellectual arguments

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r1.claim: The idols could supposedly benefit worshippers by bringing them nearer through devotion, or harm them if worship were abandoned; if they do neither, worship makes no sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p163#2/r1.anchor: أو ينفعونكم بتقربكم إليهم ودعائكم إياهم. أو يضرون بترك عبادتكم إياهم، فإذا لم ينفعوا ولم يضروا، فما معنى عبادتكم لها؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r12.claim: Some explain the idols’ benefit as provision.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p116/r13.claim: The idols might harm their worshippers if they stopped worshipping them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r3.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols benefit their worship or harm those who abandon them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:72-77/r3.anchor: على عبادتكم لها. { أو يضرون } من أعرض عنها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r3.claim: Benefit is the worshipper's primary aim; even something unable to hear might be worshipped for its own benefit or for harming an enemy, as fire can.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r3.anchor: وكان محط حال العابد والداعي بالقصد الول بالذات جلب النفع

BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r4.claim: The idols have no power to hear, benefit, or harm, as their worshippers admit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p367/r4.anchor: لا والله ! ليس عندهم شيء من ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.claim: The people concede that their idols do not hear, benefit, or harm; they follow their ancestors' practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p145#2/r4.anchor: اعترفوا بأن (1) أصنامهم لا تفعل شيئا من ذلك، وإنما رأوا آباءهم كذلك يفعلون

NAHHAS:v3p182/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p182/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p182/r6.claim: The clause is coordinated with ‘do they hear you?’

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols answer their prayers, benefit them when worshipped, or harm them if neglected.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r4.anchor: يقول: هل تجيبكم الأصنام إذا دعوتموهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r11.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols benefit or harm them, grant provision, or control good and evil; if they do neither, worship makes no sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:69-77/r11.anchor: أي هل تنفعكم هذه الأصنام وترزقكم، أو تملك لكم خيرا أو ضرا إن عصيتم

RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.claim: The reasoning is that worshippers seek help from those they worship, expecting them to hear their requests and grant benefit or avert harm; idols cannot fulfill this role.
RAZI-FULL:v24p122/r9.anchor: يلتجىء إليه في المسألة ليعرف مراده إذا سمع دعاءه ثم يستجيب له في بذل منفعة أو دفع مضرة

TABATABAI:26:70-75/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r5.claim: His second objection is that worship seeks benefit or protection from harm, while idols have no power to confer benefit or repel injury.
TABATABAI:26:70-75/r5.anchor: الناس إنما يعبدون الإله إما طمعا في خيره ونفعه وإما اتقاء من شره وضره

TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols hear their supplications, answer them, benefit them, or harm them if left; religion must rest on proof, or he would not have argued this way.
TABRISI:26:72-77/r13.anchor: معناه هل يستجيبون دعاءكم إذا دعوتموهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r6.claim: The question asks whether idols hear supplication for a desired benefit or removal of harm; they do not hear, benefit, or harm.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507/r6.anchor: {أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون} [الشعراء: 73] ، أي: هل يسمعون دعاءكم إذا دعوتموهم لرغبة يعطونكموها، أو لضراء يكشفونها عنكم، أي: أنها لا تسمع ولا تنفع ولا تضر.

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r1.claim: The idols might benefit the worshippers because they worship them; such an intense cult must be expected to bring benefit or ward off harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r1.anchor: إذ لابد للعبادة لاسيما عند كونها على ما وصفتم

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r2.claim: The object of 'harm' is omitted for the rhyme and supplied from the preceding phrase: harm you by your leaving their worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r2.anchor: أي يضرونكم بترككم لعبادتهم إذ لابد للعبادة

ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r3.claim: An alternative asks whether the idols harm anyone who turns away from their worship; Al-Alusi says this conflicts with the apparent contextual sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p94#2/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد أو يضرون من أعرض عن عبادتهم كائنا من كان وهو خلاف الظاهر

IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.claim: Qatāda explains the question as asking whether the deities answer their worshippers when called.
IBNABIHATIM:v8p2778#3/r1.anchor: وبه عن قتادة قال : هل يسمعونكم اذ تدعون ؟ هل تجيبكم الهتكم اذا دعوتموهم ؟

BURSEVI:v6p204/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r5.claim: The question asks whether the idols benefit their worshippers in return for worship.

BURSEVI:v6p204/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p204/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p204/r6.claim: It also asks whether they can harm people if worship is withheld, since worship must bring benefit or avert harm.
BURSEVI:v6p204/r6.anchor: أو يضرونكم بترك العبادة إذ لا بد للعبادة من جلب نفع أو دفع ضر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#2/r1.claim: The idols might supposedly benefit their worshippers if worshipped, or harm them if left without worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p128#2/r1.anchor: أو ينفعونكم أي إن عبدتموهم أو يضرون إن لم تعبدوهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#6/r1.claim: Ibrahim asks whether the idols benefit people if worshipped or harm them if worship is abandoned.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p188#6/r1.anchor: إن عبدتموها ﴿ أو يضرون ﴾ إن تركتم عبادتها

STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.claim: The exchange recalls 20:91, where Israelites tell Aaron they will remain devoted to their idol, and 20:97, where Moses confronts them about that devotion.
STUDYQURAN:26:71/r1.anchor: Similar language is used in 20:91, where the Israelites tell Aaron regarding their new idol

TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r1.claim: Some Basran grammarians take the question to mean whether idols hear the worshippers' invocation, with دعاء omitted, as in Zuhayr's ellipsis of حكمات before الأبق.
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعض من أنكر ذلك من قوله من أهل العربية: الفصيح من الكلام في ذلك هو ما جاء في القرآن

TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r2.speaker: بعض من أنكر ذلك من أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r2.claim: Other Arab grammarians reject that ellipsis as unnecessary: Arabs say they heard Zayd meaning his speech, while Zuhayr's prior mention of bridles licenses the later reference to the bridle without its noun.
TAB-FULL:v17p589#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض من أنكر ذلك من قوله من أهل العربية: الفصيح من الكلام في ذلك هو ما جاء في القرآن

TAB-FULL:v17p590/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r1.claim: Abraham asks whether the idols can reward worshippers with provision or harm them for neglecting worship by taking wealth or destroying them and their children.
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r1.anchor: فكان جوابهم إياه: لا، ما يسمعوننا إذا دعوناهم، ولا ينفعوننا

TAB-FULL:v17p590/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r2.claim: The reply contains an ellipsis supplied by context: the people answered that the idols neither hear them nor benefit or harm them.
TAB-FULL:v17p590/r2.anchor: فكان جوابهم إياه: لا، ما يسمعوننا إذا دعوناهم، ولا ينفعوننا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asks whether the idols provide for them, remove hardship, or can bring harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد هل يرزقونكم، أو يكشفون عنكم التفسير، أو يملكون لكم ضرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī asks whether the idols benefit them if obeyed or harm them if disobeyed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هل ينفعونكم إن أطعتموهم، أو يضرونكم إن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r3.claim: Muqātil asks whether worshipping the idols brings benefit or refusing to worship them can bring harm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p64/r3.anchor: ونحو هذا قال مقاتل: هل ينفعونكم في شيء إذا عبدتموهم، أو يضرونكم بشيء إن لم تعبدوهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.claim: The Qur'anic هل يسمعونكم إذ تدعون أو ينفعونكم أو يضرون illustrates هل followed by coordinated alternatives in a single inquiry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#516/r5.anchor: فجرى هذا مجرى قوله عز وجل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.claim: The object is omitted from harm both to suit the cadence and to leave harm general: idols cannot harm worshippers or their enemies, unlike the specified benefit they seek for themselves.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r3.anchor: والآخر: أن الإنسان يخشى من يستطعي أن يلحق به الضرر
